newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi says pensions reform talks to start.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says pensions reform talks to start.

text.p: Italy's Prime Minister Romano Prodi said that talks on reforming the pensions system should start in 1997 but needed to proceed with caution.
Prodi told reporters last night after a one-day visit to Germany: "If we are talking about getting the reform underway in 1997, that is all right."
The remarks were made to journalists on the understanding that they would not be made public until Tuesday morning.
He said that it was premature to try and predict the outcome of any talks. Italy's trade unions say the are opposed to holding any negotiations on reviewing the pensions system until 1998.

Prodi also made a comment on remarks on Monday by Massimo D'Alema, leader of the left-wing PDS party which is one of the main components of the centre-left coalition. D'Alema said that the pensions system had to be reformed this year.
"Neither D'Alema nor anyone else can anticipate the results of the discussions," said Prodi. -- Milan newsroom +392-66102321
